tools.name: list_emails
tools.description: List emails from a mail folder with optional filters (sender substring, date range, unread-only). Returns a compact JSON array of message summaries. Use read_email with a returned id to fetch full content.

folder.description: Mail folder to list. Defaults to 'inbox'. Either a well-known name (inbox, drafts, sentitems, deleteditems, junkemail, archive, outbox, conversationhistory) or a folder ID returned by list_folders. Unknown names produce a 404 from Graph — use list_folders to discover custom folders.

from.description: Filter: only emails whose sender address STARTS WITH this value (case-sensitive, Graph OData limitation). For a full domain match use 'user@acme.com' or 'acme.com'. For fuzzy / case-insensitive matching use the search_emails tool instead.

since.description: Filter: only emails received at or after this ISO-8601 timestamp (e.g. 2026-04-15T00:00:00Z).

until.description: Filter: only emails received strictly before this ISO-8601 timestamp.

unreadOnly.description: If true, return only unread messages.

limit.description: Maximum number of emails to return. Default 25, max 100.

tools.name: read_email
tools.description: Fetch the full content of one email message by id, plus a list of its attachments (metadata only — use save_attachment to write an attachment to disk). Returns JSON with body as plain text.

messageId.description: The Graph message ID (returned by list_emails or search_emails).

includeBody.description: If true, include the full body (text preferred over HTML). Default true.

tools.name: search_emails
tools.description: Full-text search across the user's ENTIRE mailbox (all folders, all years). Supports KQL-like operators: 'from:acme.com', 'subject:contract', 'hasAttachment:true', 'body:Pantheon', plus quoted phrases and AND/OR. Works on both personal (hotmail.com / outlook.com) and work/school accounts — the tool picks the correct backend automatically. IMPORTANT: results are ranked by relevance, NOT sorted by date. Date filters like 'received:this-week' are honored on AAD (work/school) but are IGNORED by the personal-account search backend, which returns matches from any time period. If you need strict date filtering, use list_emails (folder-scoped) with `since`/`until` instead. Returns a compact JSON array of hits with message IDs usable by read_email.

query.description: Full-text search query using Microsoft Graph search syntax. Examples: 'invoice from:acme.com', 'subject:contract received:this week', 'hasAttachment:true Q4 report'.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Default 25, max 250.

tools.name: save_attachment
tools.description: Download one attachment from a message and save it to the local filesystem. Writes are confined to the server's allowed directory (default ~/Downloads/outlook-mcp/). Existing files are never overwritten — the tool appends ' (2)', ' (3)', … to the filename. Returns the absolute path of the saved file.

messageId.description: The Graph message ID that contains the attachment.

attachmentId.description: The Graph attachment ID (from read_email's 'attachments' list).

targetFilename.description: Optional filename override. If omitted, the original attachment filename is used. Must be a bare filename — no path separators, no parent traversal. The destination directory is fixed by the server's OUTLOOK_MCP_ALLOWED_DIR setting and is not LLM-controllable.

tools.name: mark_email_read
tools.description: Mark a message as read or unread. Returns the updated read state. Use list_emails to find candidates; the messageId is the same opaque Graph ID returned by list_emails / search_emails / read_email.

messageId.description: The Graph message ID to update.

read.description: true to mark the message as read, false to mark it as unread.

tools.name: move_email
tools.description: Move a message into a different mail folder. The destination is either a well-known folder name (inbox, drafts, sentitems, deleteditems, junkemail, archive, outbox, conversationhistory) or a folder ID from list_folders. Returns the NEW message ID — the original ID becomes invalid after the move. To delete a message in the Outlook sense, move it to 'deleteditems' (recoverable from trash).

messageId.description: The Graph message ID to move.

destinationFolder.description: Destination mail folder. Either a well-known name (inbox, drafts, sentitems, deleteditems, junkemail, archive, outbox, conversationhistory) or a folder ID returned by list_folders. Unknown names produce a 404 from Graph — use list_folders to discover custom folders.

tools.name: list_folders
tools.description: List mail folders. With no parentFolderId, returns top-level folders. With parentFolderId set, returns immediate child folders (one level deep). Use the returned 'id' as a folder reference for list_emails or move_email. For Outlook's standard folders you can also pass their well-known names directly (inbox, drafts, sentitems, deleteditems, junkemail, archive, outbox, conversationhistory) without calling this tool first.

parentFolderId.description: If set, list the immediate children of this folder (subfolders). If omitted, list top-level folders in the user's mailbox.

limit.description: Maximum number of folders to return. Default 100, max 200.

tools.name: list_calendar_events
tools.description: List calendar events in a time window. Recurring events are expanded into individual occurrences. All returned times are in UTC — convert for display if needed. Use create_event to add a new event. `from`/`to` MUST include an explicit offset (e.g. trailing 'Z' or '+02:00') — unlike create_event, this tool has no `timeZone` parameter, so a naive (offset-less) datetime would be ambiguous and is rejected. Result is capped by `limit` (default 50, max 100); no pagination is followed, so for very busy calendars, narrow the window if you hit the cap.

from.description: Start of the time window (ISO-8601). E.g. '2026-04-22T00:00:00Z'.

to.description: End of the time window (ISO-8601, exclusive).

tools.name: create_event
tools.description: Create a calendar event. If attendees are provided, Microsoft Graph will automatically send meeting invitations. Time zone defaults to UTC if unspecified. Returns the event id and a web link to open it in Outlook.

start.description: Start time in ISO-8601. Naive (no offset) is allowed and uses timeZone; offset suffix (Z or +HH:MM) is only allowed when timeZone is UTC (or omitted).

end.description: End time in ISO-8601. Same rules as start.

timeZone.description: IANA time zone (e.g. 'Europe/Berlin'). Defaults to 'UTC' if omitted. For non-UTC zones, pass naive datetimes (no Z/offset suffix).

attendees.description: Attendees to invite. Each entry is either a bare email (treated as 'required') or {address, type} where type is 'required' | 'optional' | 'resource'. Use 'resource' for meeting rooms / equipment.

location.description: Free-text location or meeting room. Graph truncates above 256 chars.

tools.name: update_event
tools.description: Update an existing calendar event (PATCH /me/events). Only fields you pass are changed; everything else is preserved. EXCEPTION: if 'attendees' is provided, the entire attendee list is replaced — fetch the event first if you only want to add or remove individuals. Graph will email update notifications to affected attendees automatically; there is no 'silent' mode.

eventId.description: The Graph event ID to update.

start.description: New start time in ISO-8601. Naive (no offset) is allowed and uses timeZone; offset suffix is only allowed when timeZone is UTC.

end.description: New end time in ISO-8601. Same rules as start.

timeZone.description: IANA time zone (e.g. 'Europe/Berlin') for the start/end datetimes. Required if start or end uses a naive (no-offset) ISO string. Defaults to 'UTC'.

attendees.description: REPLACES the entire attendee list. Each entry is either a bare email (treated as 'required') or {address, type}. To keep existing attendees, fetch the event first, then pass the full desired list. Graph will email updates to affected attendees automatically.

tools.name: delete_event
tools.description: Delete a calendar event. DESTRUCTIVE: if the event has attendees, Microsoft Graph automatically sends a meeting cancellation to each one — there is no silent-delete mode. Solo events are simply removed. The operation is not reversible from this server. Make the implication explicit to the user before invoking. Returns the deleted event id on success.

eventId.description: The Graph event ID to delete.

tools.name: create_draft
tools.description: Create a draft email in the user's Drafts folder — NEVER sends. If replyToMessageId is set, the draft is created as a threaded reply; if `body` is provided it replaces Graph's quoted original so the caller fully controls the outgoing text. Otherwise a new standalone draft is created. The user must review and send manually in Outlook; this server has no ability to send.

body.description: Email body. Plain text by default.

replyToMessageId.description: If set, create the draft as a reply to this message (preserves thread, quotes original).
